correctness.rationale: For t>0 the Hessian of the trace exponential in a nonzero real symmetric direction is positive: in the eigenbasis of the base matrix its integral weights each squared entry of the direction by a positive factor. The edge-to-Laplacian map is injective from the off-diagonal entries, so strict convexity holds before imposing symmetry and gives a unique minimizer on the compact budget set. For every allowed edge, including at zero weight, the partial derivative is -t times the positive quadratic form of exp(-tL) on its nonzero incidence vector. Hence the budget saturates. The group generated by simultaneous vertex permutations and layer exchange is transitive on each price orbit; invariance of the unique optimum forces common a,b. The tensor sum has eigenvalues 0, 2b, ma and ma+2b with the stated multiplicities, also accounting for repeated zeros on both boundaries. For x=mta, y=2tb, log H is a sum of strictly convex functions and the constraint is (m-1)a+rb=B/m. Differentiating the reduced log trace along increasing b gives t[mr/(exp(x)+m-1)-2/(exp(y)+1)]. At b=0 the nonnegative derivative condition is exp(Bt/(m-1))<=1+m(r-1), possible only at r>1. At a=0 the feasible direction reverses sign, and the condition is exp(2Bt/(mr))<=(2-r)/r, possible only at 0<r<1. Strict convexity includes threshold equality in the appropriate disconnected phase, with a unique interior stationary solution whenever neither sign condition holds; both boundaries are excluded for r=1,t>0. A fixed connected design makes H* tend to one, so both exponentials exp(-x),exp(-y) tend to zero. Dividing the stationary equation by exp(y) gives the stated logarithmic correction; the budget fixes the common limiting ma and 2b. At r=1 the first-order expansion of the balanced exponential equation gives a-b=O(t), uniformly on the compact budget line, hence both rates tend to B/m². The two size limits follow with r,B fixed from the exact thresholds. value.rationale: This is a natural conductance-design problem in which finite-time diffusion permits disconnected optima even on a graph that can be fully connected. The unrestricted uniqueness result and two exact positive-time thresholds distinguish which of two price classes is dropped, when it reappears, and how the loss of connectivity scales with the network size. The linear versus m log m scales and the explicit recovery of long-time balance are useful information not supplied by a resistance optimum or generic convexity.
